schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE GRAMMAR EVERY LEG OF THE CHART CHAIN SPEAKS. grammar.py: where things are (CAIRN_ROOT, INSTANCE_DIR), what exists (component_roster, ref_exists — the ONE semantics, so a judge and the gate that admitted a packet can never disagree), whose voyage (ticket_path, ticket_claim_error, identity_lack — the claim rides every link), and what a packet must be (common_shape_lacks, render_lacks, CHAIN_REMEDY). chain.py: the leg vocabulary and the gate on ticket notes addressed to a leg.
why: EXTRACTED FROM ORIENT 2026-08-13, and the measurement is the argument: eight of the nine other legs imported orient, and NOT ONE touched floor_facts or validate_orient — every one took only the grammar. Stage 1 looked load-bearing for the whole chain and was not; the coupling was authorship order, not design. Left alone it made orient un-removable and made every other stage look like it needed orienting before it could check a field name. A TOOL, not a machine: it holds no durable state, so there is nothing to gate, so it has USERS and not an owner (Akien, 2026-08-13). The roster memo is a per-process memo of a measurement with an explicit forget_roster door, not a record.
invoke: imported by every chart-chain machine; `python3 -m cairn.tools.chain.chain` scans live tickets for nonconforming notes
entry: Carved out of the chart machine on 2026-08-13 under Akien's ruling — "chart is a skill, it calls a collection of machines. that's the intention." The chart charter it was carved from is the design record of the whole chain and now berths with the skill at cairn/skills/chart/intention+why.json; this file holds only what is THIS component's.
state_and_history: state.json + history.json beside this charter, born at the extraction.
gates: validate_chart_notes refuses a note addressed to a non-leg; the leg vocabulary (STAGES) has one home and this is it (Law 6).
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a second implementation of ref resolution or ticket-path lookup anywhere in the chain — two mouths that can disagree is the defect this file exists to remove; (2) this tool importing any machine (a rung inversion; it happened once, when tree.py held orient's deposit, and the move exposed it); (3) the roster memo outliving a real install in a long-lived holder without forget_roster firing — named as an IOU, not a resting state. The dial was placed here at the carve-out and moved straight back out: it imports all seven stage machines to read their AUTHORED_FIELDS, so a tool holding it would be a rung inversion seven times over. It belongs to the caller, and it now sits beside the skill's edge.
horizon: re-read when a FileChanged hook can fire forget_roster, which is the physics that retires the memo's residue.
how_it_learns: it doesn't, and that is the point: this is the fixed vocabulary the learning stages are written in. What learns are the nexi that speak it. The dial is how anyone reads whether that learning is actually compiling.
traces_to: Law 6 (one owner of the leg vocabulary)
owner: CC owns the code and proofs. A tool has users, not an owner — every chart-chain machine is a user.
proof: proofs/test_chart_notes.py, sealed by the tester; validations/ beside. The grammar itself is proved by all seven stage proofs, which cannot pass without it.
